scores.note: Hook and second line say the same thing. Merged them into one pain-plus-number opener. Timer digits on screen must be a real overlay.
'Discipline is not willpower' is the most common line in fitness content. The hook is abstract and doesn't work on mute.
Pain, a clock time and a ten-second fix, with no shame. The hook order was soft, so I moved the promise into it. Sticky note text must be a real overlay.
Runner-up. Tied on score but the bottle slot is full. 'Stop starting on Monday' would be a 9 hook if wanted later.
Best script. It says the opposite of what fitness accounts say, and it is readable on mute. The pen is shown as a tool, which is honest.
'Everyone misses this' is a stale clickbait formula. A direct visual command matches the zoom on the lid. The metal-handle fact comes from the passport.
Two tasks (toe raises, then a walk) blurred the payoff. 'Ten seconds' was also false, because five slow raises take about 20 s. Removed it.
The hook is a list, not a stopper. The 'brand slogan text overlay frame' visual risks AI-garbled brand letters.
A number formula alone is not a pain hook. Added 'Tired tonight?'. The title card '1-1-10' must be a real overlay, not generated.
Borrowed trend, vague payoff. The slogan-frame visual risks AI-broken text.
Gentle but generic. Three options means no single clear action.
Fine contrast idea but a mid hook. Split-screen visual is hard to render cleanly.
Voiceover says 'blank minutes', which sounds broken. Handwriting on screen risks garbled AI letters.
Good if-then idea, but the note reading 'IF RAIN' in the visuals risks AI-broken letters.

final.hook: Don't go to the gym tomorrow.
final.spoken: Don't go to the gym tomorrow. Take a ten minute walk instead, and carry a pen. Halfway, stop on a bench and write down one workout for Thursday. A written plan is harder to ignore than a thought. Walking counts. Planning counts. DM me PEN.
captions: Don't go to the gym tomorrow
visuals: gym door with a closed sign, wide shot
woman walking in a park path, morning light
pen clipped to a jacket pocket, close-up
woman writing in a notebook on a park bench
feet walking on a path, then a hand writing
pen resting on an open notebook, product shot
final.why: It says the opposite of what a fitness channel normally says, so the brain stops to find out why.

final.spoken: Skipped training? Ten p.m. fixes it. Stand up and write tomorrow's workout on a sticky note. Time, place, one exercise, nothing else. Then lay out your socks by the bed. You are not starting over. You are booking the next one. DM me SOCKS.
visuals: woman looking at clock late evening, sigh
clock showing ten at night on a bedside table
hand sticking a yellow note on a wall
socks laid out on a chair next to a bed
woman closing a notebook and smiling softly
socks pair product close-up on wooden floor
final.why: It names a moment of guilt and puts the promise and the clock time into the first line, so the viewer feels relief instead of blame.

final.hook: Look at the lid, not the bottle.
final.spoken: Look at the lid, not the bottle. It has a metal handle, so carrying it takes one hand and no fuss. Put the bottle by your door tonight, filled with water. Seeing it makes tomorrow's morning walk easier to start. DM me BOTTLE.
captions: Fill it. Put it by the door.
visuals: bottle in a hand, camera slowly zooming to the lid
extreme close-up of the bottle lid
metal handle on the lid, macro
woman carrying bottle by the handle while opening a door
bottle filled with water standing by a front door at night
bottle on a table, product hero shot
final.why: The command points the eye at the exact detail the zoom reveals, so the hook works even on mute.

final.spoken: Tired tonight? Try the one-one-ten reset. One glass of water. One stretch. Ten minutes of walking. Fill your bottle, take it outside, and be back before it feels like a chore. No tracking, no scoring. DM me BOTTLE.
visuals: title card on paper background: 1-1-10
glass of water being poured in a kitchen
woman stretching arms overhead in the evening
woman walking outside at sunset with a bottle
hand turning a fitness tracker face down
bottle with metal handle held in hand while walking
final.why: A tired-evening pain point plus a three-number formula gives a ready-made routine that is easy to remember.

final.hook: Missed your workout? Save today in two minutes.
final.spoken: Missed your workout? Save today in two minutes. Put your bottle by the door, set a two minute timer, and squat until it rings. Then stop. That still counts as a training day. Small and done beats big and skipped. DM me BOTTLE.
visuals: phone timer showing 2:00 close-up
woman sitting on sofa in evening light, sports clothes
metal-handle water bottle placed by a front door
woman doing bodyweight squats in a living room
kitchen timer ringing, woman smiling and stopping
hand holding bottle by the handle, product close-up
final.why: The first line names the guilt and the fix with a concrete two-minute number, readable at a glance.

final.hook: Phone down. Stand up. Right now.
final.spoken: Phone down. Stand up. Right now. Rise onto your toes five times, slowly, and lower just as slowly. That is your reset between work and workout. Then put on your socks and walk around the block. Ten minutes is plenty. DM me SOCKS.
captions: A reset between work and workout
visuals: hand putting a phone face down on a desk
woman standing up from an office chair
close-up of feet rising onto toes
woman stretching her arms by a window
woman lacing shoes over socks at the door
socks pair flat lay with KM mark on the outer side
final.why: It gives three commands the viewer can obey in the first second, and the false 'ten seconds' claim is gone.
